correctness.rationale: The two potentially clipping sides of the vertex-anchored disk have disjoint caps, and every other side misses the disk by a strict trigonometric factorization. This yields the exact area ratio and mean. Counting equally spaced angular sites gives a globally sharp count discrepancy; total variation from polygon area to disk area and a bounded limit density gives the Kolmogorov inequality. Independent polygon-clipping verification and stochastic checks passed. Boundary and n>=3 cases are explicit.

value.rationale: An exactly motivated continuous overlap-depth invariant for natural anchored diameter-disk covers has a closed mean for every polygon size, a sharp deterministic angular-discrepancy inequality, and a nondegenerate, rate-controlled limit law. It measures redundancy, not merely existence of a covering disk; full finite-n PMF and arbitrary polygons remain open.
